sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The Dragolink API is a comprehensive, enterprise-grade suite of RESTful services designed to help you integrate advanced link management, deep analytics, and dynamic QR code generation directly into your own applications.

Our API is built on standard REST principles. All URLs are predictable, resource-oriented, and strictly versioned. The API accepts standard form-encoded requests as well as JSON payloads, and returns JSON-encoded responses. We use standard HTTP response codes to indicate success or failure. Our global edge network guarantees sub-50ms latency for link resolution globally.

alert.title: API Versioning & Stability
alert.message: When we make backwards-incompatible changes to the API, we release new dated versions. The current version is 2026-08-01. You can safely pin your API version via the `Dragolink-Version` HTTP header to prevent breaking changes from affecting your production integrations.

sections.title: Authentication & Rate Limits
sections.content:
The Dragolink API uses API keys to authenticate requests. You can view, manage, and roll your API keys in the Dragolink Dashboard under Developer Settings. 

Authentication to the API is performed via HTTP Bearer Auth. You must provide your API key in the `Authorization` header of every request. All API requests must be made over HTTPS. Calls made over plain HTTP will fail. API requests without authentication will also fail.

### Rate Limiting
To ensure quality of service, the Dragolink API is rate-limited based on your subscription tier:
- **Free Tier**: 100 requests per minute
- **Pro Tier**: 1,000 requests per minute
- **Enterprise**: 10,000+ requests per second

If you exceed your rate limit, the API will return a `429 Too Many Requests` status code. You should implement an exponential backoff strategy in your SDKs to handle this gracefully. The response headers `X-RateLimit-Limit` and `X-RateLimit-Remaining` will provide exact details on your current usage.

alert.title: Keep your keys safe
alert.message: Your API keys carry full privileges to your account. Do not share your secret API keys in publicly accessible areas such as GitHub, client-side code, or public forums. If a key is compromised, immediately roll (regenerate) it in the dashboard to invalidate the old key.

sections.title: Links API
sections.content: The Links API forms the core of Dragolink. Use these endpoints to programmatically shorten long URLs, assign custom aliases, organize links with tags, implement dynamic routing rules, and set expiration parameters.

endpoints.title: Create a Link
endpoints.description: Creates a new short URL. You can optionally provide a custom alias, set an expiration date, append marketing UTM parameters, and define dynamic routing rules.

parameters.name: longUrl
parameters.description: The long URL that you want to shorten. Must be a valid URL starting with http:// or https://.

parameters.name: customAlias
parameters.description: A custom short back-half (e.g., 'summer-sale'). Leave blank for a randomly generated string. Must be unique across the domain.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: An optional internal title for your reference in the dashboard.

parameters.name: expiryDate
parameters.description: ISO 8601 timestamp for when the link should expire (e.g., '2026-12-31T23:59:59'). After this date, the link will return a 404 to visitors.

parameters.name: utmSource
parameters.description: Identifies which site sent the traffic, e.g. google, newsletter.

parameters.name: utmMedium
parameters.description: Identifies what type of link was used, e.g. cpc, email.

parameters.name: utmCampaign
parameters.description: Identifies a specific product promotion or strategic campaign.

parameters.name: routingRules
parameters.description: Array of rules for dynamic routing: {type: 'DEVICE'|'COUNTRY'|'OS', conditionValue: string, destinationUrl: string}.

endpoints.title: List Links (Paginated)
endpoints.description: Returns a paginated list of all active links in your workspace. You can filter by tags, domains, and search queries.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: The number of items per page (default: 20, max: 100).

endpoints.title: Retrieve a Link
endpoints.description: Retrieves the full details of an existing short link, including its current routing rules and click aggregates.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique Dragolink identifier of the link.

endpoints.title: Delete a Link
endpoints.description: Permanently deletes a short link. It will no longer redirect to the destination URL and will immediately return a 404 Not Found to visitors. Historical analytics data will be preserved but anonymized.

sections.title: Advanced Features (Routing & UTM)
sections.content:
Dragolink supports enterprise-grade features like UTM parameter tracking and Dynamic Contextual Routing out of the box.

### UTM Parameters
You can attach standard UTM parameters (source, medium, campaign, term, content) directly to your short links. Dragolink will automatically merge these into the final destination URL. If your destination URL already contains query parameters, Dragolink intelligently appends the UTM tags without breaking the URL structure (e.g. `?existing=1&utm_source=twitter`).

### Dynamic Routing Recipes
Dynamic routing allows you to redirect users to completely different destination URLs based on their context (Device, OS, Country, or Language) seamlessly at the edge, ensuring zero latency.

**Recipe 1: App Store Routing**
Route iOS users to the Apple App Store, and Android users to the Google Play Store. Fallback to a landing page for Desktop.
1. Set `longUrl` to `https://your-landing-page.com`
2. Add rule: `type: OS`, `conditionValue: iOS`, `destinationUrl: https://apps.apple.com/...`
3. Add rule: `type: OS`, `conditionValue: Android`, `destinationUrl: https://play.google.com/...`

**Recipe 2: Geo-Targeting (Localization)**
Route users in France to your French localized site.
1. Add rule: `type: COUNTRY`, `conditionValue: FR`, `destinationUrl: https://fr.yoursite.com`

You can define an array of `routingRules` when creating or updating a link. Rules are evaluated in order; the first matching rule triggers the redirect.

sections.title: Analytics API
sections.content: The Analytics API allows you to retrieve highly detailed, real-time metrics about your links. You can query data by time series, geographic locations (down to city-level), device types, operating systems, and referrers. Note that bots and known scrapers are automatically filtered out of all analytics aggregations to ensure your data remains completely accurate.

endpoints.title: Get Link Clicks (Time Series)
endpoints.description: Retrieves a time-series array of clicks for a specific link over a given timeframe. Data is aggregated by hour, day, or month depending on the interval parameter.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: ISO 8601 timestamp for the beginning of the reporting period.

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: ISO 8601 timestamp for the end of the reporting period.

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description: The aggregation interval. Options: 'hour', 'day', 'month'. Defaults to 'day'.

endpoints.title: Get Geographic Data
endpoints.description: Retrieves the distribution of clicks mapped to visitor countries and cities. Powered by MaxMind GeoIP2.

endpoints.title: Get Referrer Data
endpoints.description: Retrieves the distribution of clicks mapped to traffic sources (e.g., Twitter, Google, Direct, Facebook).

sections.title: QR Codes API
sections.content: Generate and manage dynamic QR codes. Dynamic QR codes can have their destination URL or routing rules changed at any time in the future without ever needing to reprint the physical QR code. All QR code scans are tracked as clicks in the Analytics API.

endpoints.title: Generate a QR Code
endpoints.description: Creates a new dynamic QR code associated with an existing link. Returns both PNG and vector SVG formats.

parameters.name: fg_color
parameters.description: The foreground color of the QR code in Hex format (e.g., '#000000'). Defaults to black.

parameters.name: bg_color
parameters.description: The background color of the QR code in Hex format (e.g., '#FFFFFF'). Defaults to transparent.

parameters.name: logo_url
parameters.description: A URL to a small image to seamlessly embed in the center of the QR code.

sections.title: Webhooks API
sections.content:
Dragolink can send webhook events that notify your application any time an event happens on your account. This is especially useful for asynchronous events—like a link being clicked or a QR code being scanned—that are not triggered by a direct API request. We guarantee at-least-once delivery with automatic retries for up to 3 days on failure.

### Verifying Signatures
All webhook payloads include a `Dragolink-Signature` header. You should use your webhook secret to compute an HMAC SHA-256 hash of the payload and compare it against the header to verify the event genuinely originated from Dragolink.

endpoints.title: Create a Webhook
endpoints.description: Registers a new webhook endpoint to receive real-time event payloads.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The HTTPS URL where Dragolink should send the webhook POST payloads.

parameters.name: events
parameters.description: An array of event types to subscribe to (e.g., ['link.clicked', 'link.created', 'qr.scanned']).

  "id": "evt_9jw3k102",

}

sections.title: Errors & Troubleshooting
sections.content:
Dragolink uses conventional HTTP response codes to indicate the success or failure of an API request. All error responses include a standard JSON payload with a specific error code, a human-readable message, and a URL pointing to detailed troubleshooting steps.

In general:
- Codes in the `2xx` range indicate success.
- Codes in the `4xx` range indicate an error that failed given the information provided (e.g., a required parameter was omitted, authentication failed, or rate limit exceeded).
- Codes in the `5xx` range indicate an error with Dragolink's servers.

errorsList.description: The request was unacceptable, often due to missing a required parameter or providing a malformed URL.
No valid API key provided. Ensure the `Authorization: Bearer <key>` header is formatted correctly.
The API key provided is valid, but it doesn't have permissions to perform the requested action (e.g., trying to access a link in a different workspace).
The requested resource doesn't exist. Verify the ID provided in the path is correct.
The request conflicts with another resource (e.g., the `customAlias` you requested is already taken by another user).
The syntax of the request is correct, but it was unable to be processed (e.g., validation failure on email format).
Too many requests hit the API too quickly. We strongly recommend implementing exponential backoff.
Something went wrong on Dragolink's end. (These are exceptionally rare, but you should gracefully retry the request).
